jobs.title: Director - Governance & Client Account Management
jobs.description:
Permanent

Department: FSD Client Management (520)

30 Adelaide Str, East

Toronto, Ontario, M5C 3G9

Canada

Number of Positions: 1

Who We Are

With its global headquarters in Toronto, Canada, International Financial Data Services (IFDS) is a world-leading provider of outsourcing and technology solutions to the financial services industry. IFDS services over 240 financial organizations around the world, providing solutions to a wide range of global asset managers, wealth managers, banks, and insurance companies. The IFDS enterprise supports more than 17 million accounts with AUA of approximately CAD $4 trillion. IFDS Canada is a 50/50 joint ventures between Boston-based State Street Corporation, one of the world’s leading providers of financial services to institutional investors, and Connecticut-based SS&C Technologies, a global provider of investment and financial software-enabled services and software for the global financial services and healthcare industries.

Imagine yourself at IFDS

Come experience a community like no other at International Financial Data Services (IFDS). We offer work opportunities driven by a passion for creating market leading financial solutions, and a culture that nurtures collaboration, accountability, diversity & inclusion, and continuous learning. We’ll provide you with opportunities to develop your career. From ongoing training and development programs to experiences working with our global financial services partners, you’ll be able to realize your full potential.

Role Overview

The Governance Director – Client Account Management provides day to day oversight; guidance and strategic leadership to our client and the broader support team at IFDS and SS&C through close collaboration with the Business Development Relationship Manager, the AMS team, IT Departments; the Business Solutions and Planning team and C-Suite individuals to ensure the delivery of superior service commitments aligned with client goals. The incumbent will own the overall oversight of key initiatives and changes impacting the client, identifying risks and issues and will be responsible for the timely closure of all remediation actions. The Director will provide guidance and leadership, coaching and development to managers and employees to ensure that clients are supported with high quality solutions tailored to their business needs.

Governance

Role Responsibilities

Oversee a virtual support team consisting of both IFDS and SS&C individuals dedicated to the overall successful delivery of changes.
Build and maintain a governance practice consisting of key reporting and metrics tracking all initiatives/changes / issues - identifying and addressing risks and issues to continuously enhance service, client relationships and improve operational efficiencies.
Acts as an escalation point for the client re any key changes.
Lead the identification and documentation of risks and controls across changes and initiatives (projects, service requests, incidents and adhoc initiatives such as proactive testing of complex functionality).
Elevate the profile and product knowledge of clients by providing deep expertise in risk and controls in conjunction with virtual support team.
Implement an internal/ external forum/s to meet regularly with the “virtual” support teams (and the client) to provide and discuss status of changes/issues and hold teams accountable to timely resolution and remediation actions.
Ongoing assessment of venues / documentation and ensures all processes serve a key purpose and align with client and IFDS requirements. E.g. any “special client reporting” from CAMs – Vendor Scorecard; Usage reporting; Utilization reporting etc. Delivers to client (along with new findings/solutions etc)
Ongoing review processes/operating model etc. to ensure “we evolve our processes and engagement” aligned with iA’s evolution in business growth and strategy
Overseas the SLA adherence and smooth delivery of client requests, to ensure delivery is in accordance with client expectations
Work directly with the client and internal teams to ensure clarity and organization of all changes and release/ delivery dates.
Develop and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders, business partners to ensure effective collaboration and communication.
Drive change management initiatives, guiding the team through evolving operational risk management standards and expectations.
Foster a team environment and culture that encourages productivity, innovation, process improvement, and professionalism.

Account Management Service Delivery

Oversees day-to-day issue resolution and all critical reoccurring processes for clients, which includes planning and execution of the overall client service delivery experience in collaboration with all internal and external clients to oversee the delivery of superior customer service in alignment with the client’s strategic goals 
Interacts directly with key business partners, developing and maintaining a strong on-going relationship; always looking for opportunities to improve client satisfaction and experience
Facilitates and leads various internal / client meetings (virtually and / or in person) as it relates to the mandate and participates in all key reoccurring meetings regarding TLR; Release Management; JAD sessions; client reviews
Oversees the various aspects of client business operations, regulatory, statutory and industry standards bodies to understand and ensure appropriate and timely communication of business requirements for client consumption in collaboration with internal and external teams
Acts as an escalation point for Client Account Managers on incidents/service requests and the client if resolution is not attained timely / accurately
Supports Business Development & Relationship Management with new product onboarding opportunities as required.

Leadership and People Management

Completes performance reviews; successions plans; establishing objectives in monitoring performance against plans; promotes training and professional development. Works closely with Human Resources on talent management
Provides performance feedback, coaching, mentoring and career and development planning for team members
Ensures continued employee engagement by promoting an “in the office presence” through participation in IFDS events; team meetings and events; internal working groups
Reviews current operating procedures, revising and implementing changes to improve service levels, productivity and cost effectiveness
Maintains current knowledge of financial; regulatory and operational issues affecting other departments and the company as a whole. Understands financial and operational goals of IFDS
Provides the team with support and recommendations on project prioritization and resource management
Oversees and provides the team guidance and direction with new opportunities with the development and discussion of operational enhancements to improve the client experience which may include but not limited to guidance with approach; test strategy and developing test plan and cases
Oversees and provides the team guidance and direction with new processes, policies and special initiatives as needed to enhance and support business needs.
Assists VP Account Management with salary administration; capacity planning and staffing plans

Minimum Qualifications

Demonstrated superior leadership skills including collaboration; relationship building; coaching; integrity; resilience to a fast paced; high stress environment; ownership and accountability, credibility, and consensus building
Demonstrated proficiency in communicating complex business solutions with clients & internal stakeholders
Solid technical knowledge of IFDS applications (including iFast, IFWP, etc).
Good knowledge of Segregated Fund, RESP, GIA/DIA, Guarantee Fee, FHSA product/iFast functionality.
Strong Change Management capability (ADKAR)
Highly analytical with a very high degree of attention to detail
Strong research / information gathering / analytical and problem-solving skills - takes a logical approach to analyzing problems. Systematically researches information and explores alternatives to solve problems.
Post-secondary education in a related discipline
Minimum 10 years’ experience in the financial service industry in a client facing, relationship management or Operational capacity
Minimum 10 years’ experience in leadership/people management
Solid knowledge of financial mutual fund record keeping systems and transfer agency operations
In depth knowledge of the mutual fund and banking industry of financial investment markets, trends and competitive framework
Understanding of investment concepts and the ability to communicate a working knowledge of investment strategies and products
High level of competency with MS suite, including but not limited to; Excel, Visio, Word, Powerpoint.
Superior communication verbal and written skills, as well as high level of interpersonal skill to interact with senior business professionals
Ability to engage internal stakeholders across a number of different functional areas
Strong quantitative, analytical and problem solving/troubleshooting skills combined with the ability to draw meaningful conclusions from qualitative client feedback or large data sets
Demonstrated ability to innovate and develop new proposals/solutions
Ability to manage direct and indirect reports in a virtual team setting
Proven project management skills, with strong attention to detail and flexibility to handle multiple projects and changing priorities
Enthusiastic and proactive approach with meticulous attention to detail
Extensive experience working with IFDS tools and clients (understands the full picture) Able to handle or lead (as appropriate)complex projects major change

AODA Statement

IFDS Canada encourages applications from all qualified individuals. Applicants with disabilities may notify us of any accommodation needed to support your participation in the recruitment process. We wish to thank all applicants for their interest and effort in applying. Please be aware that only candidates selected for interviews will be contacted for this position.

Salary Range

Pay Range (CAD $): 126,000 - 159,000

The above reflects an industry-benchmarked target compensation range. The salary offered may vary based upon the candidate’s skills and experience, job-related knowledge, and other specific business needs.

IFDS Provides

Total Rewards: IFDS offers a comprehensive, competitive compensation & benefits package
Work-Life Balance: IFDS offers a hybrid work environment with our office located in the downtown core within walking distance to Union Station and the PATH
Professional Development: IFDS offers continuous learning opportunities, leadership development & training programs
Inclusive Culture: Our inclusive work environment supports equity and values diversity
Wellness Programs: Access to a variety of wellness initiatives, mental health support, and employee assistance programs
Community Engagement: Participate in volunteer opportunities and give back to our community through our various social care programs

Client Experience Operations

jobs.title: Vice President (Head) of Finance
jobs.description:
Our client is a highly respected, mission-driven not-for-profit organization dedicated to improving well-being and quality of life in the communities it serves. The organization is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Vice President, Finance to join its Executive Leadership Team. Reporting to the CEO, the Vice President will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As Vice President, Finance, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the Vice President will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VP will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the VP will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Using financial insights and performance data, the VP will help evaluate opportunities, inform strategic initiatives, and optimize the deployment of resources in a complex funding and operating environment. Success will require balancing long-term vision with disciplined execution and sound financial management.

Beyond finance, the VP will provide executive oversight of key corporate services, including procurement and facilities, ensuring effective stewardship of organizational resources and infrastructure. The role will also lead efforts to strengthen internal capabilities, foster collaboration across departments, and build a high-performing, engaged team.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to evolve the finance function from a trusted service provider into an even more proactive strategic partner and to enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. Success will be measured not only by financial outcomes, but also by the ability to influence strategy, support growth, and contribute to long-term sustainability and impact.

Leadership and Stewardship

The organization is seeking a VP Finance who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. The culture here rewards people who show up prepared, communicate clearly, and follow through.
Operates with humility, credibility, and sound judgment
Brings a practical, solutions-oriented mindset
Communicates clearly and influences at all levels
A good partner to the program managers – asking what they need before explaining what the number say
Leads with integrity, accountability, and transparency

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will bring experience in social services, healthcare, the boarder public sector, or the not-for-profit sector. Those who understand the operational, funding, and stakeholder dynamics of publicly funded organizations will be particular well positioned for success.
A CPA designation and progressive senior finance leadership experience.
Experience leading finance within a complex, multi-stakeholder organization.
A strong understanding of financial planning, financial reporting, treasury, governance, risk management, and internal controls.
Experience working with Boards and senior executives in a strategic advisory capacity.
The ability to translate financial information into actionable business insights.
A collaborative leadership style and a reputation for building strong relationships across an organization.

Why This Role

This is a rare opportunity to combine executive-level impact with genuine purpose. As a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Vice President, Finance will help shape decisions that influence the organization’s direction, sustainability, and growth.

The successful candidate will join an organization at an exciting point in its journey, with the opportunity to strengthen financial stewardship, support strategic priorities, and help position the organization for continued success. The organization measures its success not only by financial performance, but by the positive impact it has on the people and communities it serves.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact and help shape the future of a mission-driven organization, we encourage you to apply in confidence.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer - Highly Engineered Design/Manufacturing- Private Equity, 79074
jobs.description:
Chief Financial Officer - Highly Engineered Design/Manufacturing - Private Equity

Our client is a designer and manufacturer of highly engineered products for the scientific and industrial marketplace undergoing significant growth under private equity ownership. We are seeking a Chief Financial Executive to partner with the CEO and management team to catapult the business to the next level.

You will be working to an aggressive growth strategy, with both acquisitive and organic growth initiatives, and will be deeply involved at a strategic and tactical level working as a valued member of the executive team. You will oversee the finance, accounting, and information technology teams and be accountable for building a robust and scalable process platform.

This will be a “roll up your sleeves” environment, where you will be involved in the details as well as at the strategic level. Key mandates are to upgrade financial reporting and operational KPI dashboards, overhaul systems for cost accounting and inventory management, and manage due diligence and integration plans for new acquisitions.

The ideal candidate will have a combination of the following experiences: manufacturing industry experience, multi-location and global jurisdiction experience, working with a leveraged balance sheet, managing bank relationships, acquisitions and integration.

A base salary in the $250K - $300K range with additional bonus and equity is offered.

About Osara Health
Osara Health is a digital health company that empowers people and organizations impacted by cancer to thrive through expertise, empathy, and technology. Our health coaching programs improve clinical outcomes for both patients and caregivers across the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.

Job Description
We are looking for a leader to join the team as our Head of Customer Strategy.
Reporting to the co-founder, this role will lead Osara Health’s key customer partnerships across the US and Canada, with a particular focus on large enterprise insurers and employers. In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring our customers thrive with Osara Health’s products and services by building strong executive relationships, driving member and employee engagement, delivering measurable value, and identifying opportunities to deepen and grow our partnerships.
You will lead the North American customer day to day operations, shaping our approach to strategic account management and helping establish the capabilities required to support a growing portfolio of enterprise customers.
This is a highly visible and externally facing leadership role, combining strategic customer leadership with a strong focus on partnership success, engagement and growth 

Roles and responsibilities
Lead the NA Customer Success function:
Guide strategic account planning and ensure strong customer relationships, engagement, and retention across North America. Take responsibility for customer success outcomes, including high satisfaction, timely renewals, and identifying upsell opportunities.
Drive customer engagement and impact:
Develop and execute strategies to increase awareness, engagement and utilisation of Osara Health programs across customer populations, working closely with customers to improve program performance and outcomes.
Build executive-level relationships:
Develop trusted partnerships with senior stakeholders across large enterprise insurers and employers, becoming a strategic advisor and senior point of contact for Osara Health’s key accounts.
Scale processes and leverage technology:
Set up and continuously improve Customer Success processes, incorporating new workflows and implementing modern technologies to increase efficiency and enhance the customer experience. Analyse data to identify trends, measure performance, and optimize growth initiatives.
Champion the voice of the customer:
Bring customer insights and feedback into Osara Health, working cross-functionally with Product, Marketing, Clinical, Data and Business Development teams to continuously improve our offering and customer experience.
Represent Osara Health externally (travel as needed):
Represent Osara Health in executive meetings, business reviews and industry events, with travel across North America as required to build relationships and support partnership success.

Skills & Experience
3 years in professional services (law, banking, consulting)
Experience working with large enterprise clients
High attention to detail
Strong at developing and maintaining relationships
Relevant university degree
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
Ability to multitask, prioritise, and manage time effectively.
Strong data analysis and interpretation skills
Comfortable working in a remote team environment.

Renumeration
Annual salary range: CAD $150-170k base, based on skills, experience and location.

Benefits
Established remote-first working culture
Be a part of fast-growing company making a major impact in healthcare, improving the lives of people living with cancer or caring for someone with cancer
8 weeks paid parental leave for primary and secondary carers
Flexible working arrangements
Annual budget for professional development

Why Osara Health
Great team and company culture with 50+ close-knit team members who are down to earth, hardworking, and kind.
Opportunity to contribute to a startup with a social purpose.
We carefully hire the best talent, actively seeking diversity of beliefs, backgrounds, education, and ways of thinking. We strive to build an inclusive culture where differences are celebrated and leveraged to inform better design and business decisions. Osara Health is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We are committed to equal opportunity regardless of race, colour, religion, sex, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, family care status, marital status, sexual orientation, or any other basis protected by commonwealth laws.

About Osara Health:
Osara Health was founded in 2015 by cancer specialists to transform the experience of living with cancer. We build support programs and technology designed to support and empower people impacted by cancer. We believe strongly in the power that positive healthy behaviors can have on clinical outcomes, which is why we aspire to be the leaders in behaviour change.
